claims.content: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory products using combinable filtering/search criteria.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory products using combinable filtering/search criteria.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer browses the auction inventory, enters or selects one or more search/filter criteria, and gets a filtered set of matching products to review.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer initiates a browse or search over auction inventory items.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer is able to view products that match the selected search/filter criteria.
in_scope_actions: Search products using criteria such as Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, Cost Range
Filter results by criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location

claims.content: Customer
Inventory data is populated and available in the system for the Auctioneer to access.

The Customer initiates the use case by using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the inventory, or by entering a Product ID (e.g., ABC123) or Customer Email Address and clicking 'Go', or by selecting search parameters such as Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range and clicking 'Find Product'.
The Customer browses the auction inventory using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability.

The Customer enters or selects one or more search/filter criteria, such as Product ID (wildcards * or % allowed), low/high cost range, or multiple filters from scrolling list boxes for Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, and Brand.
The Customer clicks the 'Go' or 'Find Product' button to execute the search.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing matching auction items and thumbnail images.
The Customer reviews the matching products and may sort the results by clicking underlined column headers or further refine them using autofilter functions similar to Excel.

Diverges from Step 1: instead of initiating the browse through the Endeca search/navigation capability, the Customer may access the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists all available Categories (Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages, then continue to review matching products.

Diverges from Step 1: instead of initiating the browse through dynamic filters or search forms, the Customer may enter product browsing via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types (e.g., 'tanzanite page') or product types (e.g., 'Rings page'), which contain direct links to relevant product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.
The Customer may include a scope filter in the search criteria by choosing, via radio buttons, between 'Items currently online only' and 'All sellable auction inventory'.
The Customer may include combinable visibility filters by choosing, via radio buttons, to show items with or without images, or with or without a valid (sellable) location.
Diverges from Step 5: while reviewing the product results, the Customer may switch between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes.

The Customer may group results using a scrolling list box with options such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; each grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from Step 5: rather than sorting only by clicking underlined column headers, the Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence that this action is performed by the 'Customer' (the cited cards describe the report's capabilities without specifying the actor).
Explicit evidence that this action is performed by the 'Customer' (the cited card describes the report's functionality without specifying the actor).

claims.content: Diverges from main flow Step 1: If the Customer clicks a link/category that contains no product (e.g., collectibles routinely have no product), the system serves a 'No Results Found' page. Exit: branch outcome is the 'No Results Found' page.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: If the search results in no matches (e.g., for the term 'belly button'), the system displays a 'No Results Found' page that includes: (1) an apology message stating no matches were found; (2) a 'Search Tips' section with five specific suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support); and (3) a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section containing static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data. Exit: branch outcome is the 'No Results Found' page.

Diverges from main flow Step 4: If matching products have no available image, the system prevents them from appearing in search results/catalog pages; this pre-filter can produce an empty result set even though other criteria matched. Exit: branch outcome is the image pre-filter applied (empty/incomplete result set).

Diverges from main flow Step 5: If the Customer is not signed in and clicks anywhere within a product module (except the QuickBid button), the system presents a sign-in page, requires the Customer to complete sign-in, and then delivers the Customer to the Product Details page. Exit: after sign-in, continue to the Product Details page.

missing_aspects: No documented continuation from the 'No Results Found' page back to the main flow or to termination for empty-category-link and zero-match exceptions.
No documented system response (e.g., whether the 'No Results Found' page is shown) when the image pre-filter eliminates all matching products.

claims.content: The system displays search results with columns in this default order: Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type (e.g., Ring, Single Stone), and Increment.

When the Customer selects Catalog View for the filtered product list, the system displays Product Modules, each containing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format showing time remaining, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger only describes search-form initiation (entering Product ID/Email or search parameters and clicking Go/Find Product), but Main Flow step 1 starts with 'The Customer browses the auction inventory using Endeca'. This is a different initiation path, so the Main Flow does not logically continue from the Trigger; it restarts as a browse scenario. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (EC-MF-005 supports a main-flow browsing action, not an explicit trigger; it also does not support 'auction inventory'.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The trigger is initiated by the Customer using the Customer-facing Endeca/Endeca-like search-and-navigation capability or product/email/parameter search, but the sole precondition states only that inventory data is populated and available in the system for the Auctioneer to access. It does not establish that the Customer-facing browse/search path has access to the populated inventory data before the trigger, so the preconditions-to-trigger coverage is broken by an actor mismatch.

inconsistency_hints: Postcondition 2 claims the system displays Product Modules (thumbnail, description, countdown timer, high bid, QuickBid), but the Main Flow only reaches the Search Results table in step 4. The browse action in step 1 is not specified as displaying Product Modules, so this postcondition is not reachable from the Main Flow.

The Trigger only covers explicit search initiation (entering a Product ID/email or selecting search parameters and clicking Go/Find Product). Main Flow step 1 instead starts with 'Customer browses the auction inventory using Endeca', which is a separate browse entry point that was not fired by the Trigger. This makes the Main Flow restart with a different scenario rather than continue from the Trigger.
